study_label: Immunosuppression versus supportive therapy for idiopathic membranous nephropathy

objective.value: To test whether immunosuppressive therapy with prednisolone plus chlorambucil or ciclosporin preserves renal function compared with supportive therapy alone in patients with idiopathic membranous nephropathy and declining renal function.

population.value: Adults aged 18–75 years with biopsy-proven idiopathic membranous nephropathy, creatinine less than 300 μmol/L, and at least a 20% decline in excretory renal function documented over at least 3 months within the previous 2 years. Patients with secondary membranous nephropathy and specified infections, malignancy, treatments, pregnancy-related, or prior-treatment-reaction exclusions were excluded. Participants were recruited from 37 UK renal units.

intervention.value: Two immunosuppressive regimens added to supportive therapy: (1) 6 months of prednisolone and chlorambucil, including intravenous methylprednisolone and oral prednisolone during months 1, 3, and 5 and oral chlorambucil during months 2, 4, and 6; or (2) 12 months of ciclosporin starting at 5 mg/kg/day and adjusted to trough concentrations of 100–200 μg/L. Supportive therapy included renin-angiotensin blockade, statins, and anticoagulants as indicated.

comparator.value: Supportive therapy alone, including renin-angiotensin blockade, statins, and anticoagulants as indicated.

duration_follow_up.value: Patients were followed until the primary endpoint occurred or, if it did not occur, for a minimum of 3 years. Prednisolone plus chlorambucil was administered for 6 months and ciclosporin for 12 months.

primary_outcome.value: A further 20% decline in excretory renal function from baseline, calculated with the Cockcroft-Gault equation.

effect_result.value: For the primary endpoint, prednisolone plus chlorambucil significantly reduced risk versus supportive therapy: 19/33 (58%) versus 31/37 (84%); HR 0.44 (95% CI 0.24–0.78), p=0.0042. Ciclosporin did not differ significantly from supportive therapy: 29/36 (81%) versus 31/37 (84%); HR 1.17 (95% CI 0.70–1.95), p=0.54. The three-group comparison was significant (p=0.003).

safety.value: There were 390 adverse events, including 117 serious events in 54 patients. By 1 year, serious adverse events were significantly more frequent with prednisolone plus chlorambucil than supportive therapy (17/33 [52%] versus 11/38 [29%]; p=0.048); ciclosporin did not differ significantly from supportive therapy (17/37 [46%] versus 11/38 [29%]; p=0.20). Deaths did not differ significantly between groups, and none were classified as likely treatment-related. Malignant disease was reported in 2/33 (6.1%) patients receiving prednisolone plus chlorambucil.

sample_size.analyzed: 106 (intention-to-treat: supportive therapy 37; prednisolone plus chlorambucil 33; ciclosporin 36)
sample_size.planned: 116 recruited (105, or 35 per group, before allowing for 10% dropout)

evidence_questions.objective: In adults with idiopathic membranous nephropathy and declining renal function, does prednisolone plus chlorambucil added to supportive therapy preserve renal function compared with supportive therapy alone?
evidence_questions.population: Adults aged 18–75 years with biopsy-proven idiopathic membranous nephropathy, creatinine less than 300 μmol/L, and documented declining excretory renal function.
evidence_questions.intervention: Supportive therapy plus 6 months of prednisolone and chlorambucil.
evidence_questions.primary_outcome: Further 20% decline in excretory renal function from baseline.

evidence_questions.objective: In adults with idiopathic membranous nephropathy and declining renal function, does ciclosporin added to supportive therapy preserve renal function compared with supportive therapy alone?
evidence_questions.population: Adults aged 18–75 years with biopsy-proven idiopathic membranous nephropathy, creatinine less than 300 μmol/L, and documented declining excretory renal function.
evidence_questions.intervention: Supportive therapy plus 12 months of ciclosporin.
evidence_questions.primary_outcome: Further 20% decline in excretory renal function from baseline.
